scope: SEEDED RANDOM SUBSET of 5 pairs (seed 11) -- SCOPE reduction, no n600 verdict
question: Is PoseNet's sensitivity to a band edit spatially uniform, or is there a region where a free pixel actuator is affordable in pose?
method: guided at tau=8, band-local, restricted to the camera band pixels whose own token class is c, one class at a time. Frozen CPU scorer on the retained renders. baseline d_pose 5.1845e-06, baseline seg errors 92.
class_order_note: canonical comma10k order 0=Road 1=Lane 2=Undrivable 3=Movable 4=MyCar, per CLAUDE.md; never the luma sort
finding: The pose tax per edited pixel varies 30x across class bands. It is concentrated in Road (0.0691 S per 1000 px) and Undrivable (0.1259) -- exactly the regions that carry the ego-motion geometry -- and is 16x to 30x lower on the static ego hood MyCar (0.0042) and on Lane markings (0.0095). PoseNet is not uniformly sensitive to the frame; it is sensitive to the ground plane and the horizon.
but: delta_S_seg is POSITIVE in every band, including the cheap ones. The Lane band is the sharpest case: it carries 44% of the residual (Road<->Lane is 5,365 of 12,196 errors) and is pose-cheap, yet it shows the LARGEST seg harm of any band (+0.003764) from only 4,654 edited pixels. So the spatial escape does not rescue this family either.
handoff: For any successor building a receiver-side pixel actuator on this vehicle: the pose channel is affordable only inside the MyCar and Lane bands, and a Road or Undrivable edit is 7x to 30x more expensive per pixel. But the seg channel is harmful in EVERY band, so a successor actuator must be seg-positive BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely pose-cheap. Widen this 5-pair arm to a seeded RANDOM n>=120 before routing on it.
